draft.title: Confucius and Chinese beliefs
card: Confucius was a teacher who lived in China about 2,500 years ago. He taught that a good society depends on people doing their duties and showing respect.
He taught respect for family, for elders and for rulers. Children should honour their parents, and rulers should set a good example for their people.
These ideas shaped Chinese government and daily life for many centuries. Officials were expected to be educated and to behave well.
Daoism taught people to live in harmony with nature. Many families also honoured their ancestors with offerings and care for their memory.
draft.remember: Confucius taught respect for family, elders and rulers, and Daoism and ancestor honouring were part of Chinese life too.

opts: People should respect their family, elders and rulers
People should live apart from society and follow nature
People should honour only the gods and not their parents
People should choose their ruler by a vote each year
a.why: Confucius taught respect for family, elders and rulers. Living in harmony with nature is the Daoist idea, so it is tempting but belongs to a different set of beliefs.
a.clue: Think about the duties people owed each other.

b.q: A village in ancient China treats its oldest members with great respect and asks their advice before big decisions. Which belief does this best show?
opts: The Confucian teaching of respect for elders
The Daoist teaching of living in harmony with nature
The Mandate of Heaven being taken from a ruler
The honouring of ancestors with offerings at a shrine
b.why: Respect for elders is a Confucian teaching, and the villagers are showing it to living people. Honouring ancestors is about family members who have died, so it does not fit a village asking living elders for advice.
b.clue: Are the elders in this story living or dead?

a.best: People should respect their family, elders and rulers

b.best: The Confucian teaching of respect for elders
